Skill patch (officeqa-treasury-bulletin/SKILL.md, new section "Expected Shortfall / VaR at X% — historical portfolio return approach"):
- Historical/empirical method: VaR@95% = 5th-percentile of the yearly-value sample; Expected Shortfall (CVaR) = mean of values at/below that percentile. No Gaussian z-score.
- Build sample as one cell per year over the inclusive span; raw yield levels ARE the "returns" (don't difference unless asked).
- Small-N quirk (N≈10): 5th percentile ≈ the minimum, so ES ≈ min of the series.
- Sign convention: report the tail mean as NEGATIVE (loss sign). Right magnitude + wrong sign = flip needed. Worked example -18.51 graded CORRECT even without the gold's trailing '%'.
- Source-table note: New Aa/Aaa corporate yields = Bulletin capital-market interest-rate exhibit (Moody's seasoned corporate rows), read the Jan row per year.
